rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so weights are pushed toward stronger obfuscation. This is a small (14 KB text, 30 functions) dense numeric/eigenvalue benchmark dominated by arithmetic-heavy loops (Jacobi, QRiterate, Trianglelise, DivideAndSolve), so SUB gets the highest weights: instruction substitution is nearly free at runtime/size yet directly obscures the floating-point and integer kernels, and its low correctness risk suits loop-heavy code. FLA is next strongest since the large functions have substantial control flow to flatten, with moderate cost weighting to protect the hot iterative solvers. BCF is kept at solid but not maximal security weight with elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so the dispatcher junk is steered away from the innermost numeric loops, bounding blowup in a binary that is already tiny. SPLIT is favored modestly as a cheap diversity amplifier that composes well with FLA. IBR and ICALL get mid-range security weights with meaningful cost/risk weights: this code has few indirect call sites and branch-heavy loops where indirection hurts most, so they apply selectively. IGV is moderately enabled because the benchmark relies heavily on global matrices/vectors, giving decent coverage at low risk. Nothing is disabled since round 0 showed the full pipeline is safe here; the cost weights simply gate the expensive passes to where the payoff justifies the overhead.
